title: Policy engine: guardrails + approvals for Hosted canary rollout actions
creator: Ethan Park
description:
Context
We’re adding GA-ready Hosted canary rollout workflow in Console. The Console backend/orchestrator will call the policy engine before allowing any rollout action (create, start, advance step, pause, resume, rollback, cancel). This ticket implements the policy checks + consistent error surface so Console can show clear guardrail messaging.

Scope
1) Action authorization (RBAC / actor + tenant context)
- Enforce that only principals with the right permission can:
  - create_rollout
  - start_rollout
  - advance_rollout_step
  - pause_rollout / resume_rollout
  - rollback_rollout
  - approve_rollout_step (approval gate)
- Integrate with rollout-approver role from policy bundle (see rbac-policy-bundle PR-311). Goal: separate “operator” vs “approver”.

2) Guardrails on rollout schedule and step transitions
- Max step size (percentage point delta) (tenant-configurable; default enforced if unset).
- Min soak time between step changes (tenant-configurable; default enforced if unset).
- Approval gate semantics:
  - Some tenants require explicit approval before increasing canary traffic beyond a configured threshold (e.g., >10%) or for every step.
  - Approval can be required for: start, advance step, or rollback-from-canary-to-baseline (optional; see open question).
- Block unsafe configs: total traffic must sum to 100, canary percent must be within allowed range for the action.

3) Error model for Console
- Return consistent, customer-safe errors from policy engine for:
  - forbidden action (RBAC)
  - violates_max_step
  - violates_min_soak_time
  - requires_approval
  - invalid_rollout_state / invalid_action_for_state
- Include actionable message and a stable code for Console to map to inline validation.

Non-goals
- Quality-gate automation (future).
- Dedicated/Private policy parity (but keep schema compatible).

Policy inputs
The policy engine will receive:
- tenant_id, actor_id, actor_type (user/service), actor_roles
- route_id, environment (hosted), region_scope (for messaging only)
- rollout_id + current rollout state (draft/running/paused/rolled_back/completed)
- current_step (baseline/canary split), proposed_action + proposed_target_percent (if relevant)
- timestamps (created_at, last_step_change_at, last_approval_at)
- tenant rollout policy config (defaults + overrides):
  - max_step_pct_points (default 25)
  - min_soak_minutes (default 30)
  - approval_required (none | beyond_threshold | every_step)
  - approval_threshold_percent (default 10)

Acceptance criteria
- Any call from orchestrator to perform a rollout action is denied if:
  - actor lacks required permission for that action
  - proposed percent jump exceeds max_step_pct_points
  - time since last_step_change_at < min_soak_minutes (for advance step; also for start if tenant chooses)
  - approval gate is configured and no valid approval exists for the action/step
- Policy engine returns structured denial information:
  - code: one of (rbac_forbidden, rollout_max_step_exceeded, rollout_min_soak_time_not_met, rollout_approval_required, rollout_invalid_state)
  - message: customer-safe string usable in Console
  - details: short string intended for internal logs only (still string; no secrets)
- Console backend can map errors directly to:
  - inline validation on wizard schedule builder (max step / min soak)
  - “Request approval” UX when approval_required
- Unit tests cover:
  - step size boundaries (exactly equal allowed; > denied)
  - min soak boundaries (exactly equal allowed; less denied)
  - approval flow (approve then allow)
  - RBAC differences (operator cannot approve; approver cannot edit schedule unless also operator)

Implementation notes
- Policy evaluation order (per ADR):
  1) hard RBAC deny
  2) invalid action for rollout state
  3) guardrails (max step, soak)
  4) approval gates
  5) allow
- Ensure deny semantics are explicit and deterministic (first matching denial code returned).
- Treat auto-stop/rollback actions as “system actor” and bypass approval gate, but still enforce state validity. (Guardrails for auto-rollback are enforced by stop-condition component, not policy engine.)

Open questions
- Should rollback require approval for approval_required=every_step tenants? Product leaning: NO (rollback should be fast), but some regulated customers may want it. Proposal: default no approval for rollback; allow tenant override later.
- Should pause/resume require approvals? Proposal: no, only operator permission.

Rollout plan
- Feature flag in Console controls exposure; policy engine must be deployed ahead of enabling for beta tenants.
- During beta, ship with conservative defaults (max_step=25, min_soak=30m) and allow tenant overrides via internal config.

Risks
- Confusing messaging if we surface internal state names. Mitigation: messages must be phrased in customer terms ("This step increases canary traffic by 30%, which exceeds your org’s max allowed increase of 25%"), and include next action ("Reduce step size or request an override from an admin").
- Approval flow edge cases (multiple pending approvals, approvals that apply to a specific target percent). Mitigation: approval object should include target_percent and expiry; policy checks for an approval matching the proposed action + target.

Owner / reviewers
- Owner: Jordan Lee
- Reviewers: Ethan Park, Kaitlyn Nguyen (RBAC integration), Marcus Lin (audit/governance), Dylan Brooks (Console error UX)
comments: 2025-02-06 (Jordan Lee): Started design for rollout policy rules. Aligning with PM-1851 guardrails and mapping to permissions in RBAC bundle. Will return stable denial codes for Console mapping.

2025-02-10 (Kaitlyn Nguyen): Please ensure we distinguish user vs service principals. For service-to-service orchestrator calls, actor is still the end-user via delegated auth; system actions (auto-rollback) should be an explicit system actor to avoid privilege escalation.

2025-02-13 (Marcus Lin): Approval gate must be auditable. Even though audit events are in ENG-9171, policy should return enough context for orchestrator to log why it was denied (without leaking policy config). Also ensure error messages don’t expose internal role names; use “admin/approver” language.
2025-02-18 (Jordan Lee): Implemented rule ordering per ADR. Added denial codes and customer-safe messages. Pending decision on rollback approval requirement (default no).

2025-02-24 (Ethan Park): Confirmed with Paula/Marissa: rollback must not require approval for GA; keep room for future tenant override. Also confirm min-soak applies only to advance step (not pause/resume).
2025-03-03 (Jordan Lee): PR up: pr-28802. Includes unit tests and wiring in policy engine client used by orchestrator. Needs Console team to verify message copy fits wizard UI.

2025-03-07 (Dylan Brooks): Console wants stable field names in error payload. If we can’t add structured JSON, please keep message formatting consistent and include numeric values (requested_delta, max_delta, remaining_soak_minutes) in the message text so UI can display them.

2025-03-12 (Jordan Lee): Updated messages to include requested/allowed values and remaining soak time in minutes. Added specific code for approval_required. Waiting on final RBAC permission names from PR-311 merge.
2025-03-19 (Benji Okafor): Noted edge case: if tenant policy config missing (null), we should apply defaults, not allow. Added fallback defaults in policy evaluation context builder.
2025-03-21 (Jordan Lee): Moved to In Review. Need final approval from Security on wording and from Console on error mapping. After merge, we should run through beta tenant enablement checklist.
